hero.subtitle: World developments, Nigeria politics, security, diplomacy, business and technology.

headline: Ukraine attack, Belgium political uncertainty, Hormuz tensions and Nigeria's electoral integrity debate dominate global developments.
intro: Good evening. This is the RadiantWaves Media global news update for Monday, 2 November 2026. Tonight's coverage examines the latest developments in Ukraine, growing uncertainty over the Strait of Hormuz, political changes in Europe, Nigeria's electoral register review and the accountability questions facing political leaders ahead of the country's next election cycle.
morningSummary: International attention remains focused on the war in Ukraine and tensions around the Strait of Hormuz. Belgium's prime minister has offered his resignation following a coalition budget disagreement, while Nigeria's electoral commission is reviewing 268 preliminary voter-register records flagged for suspected irregularities. In Nigeria, public procurement oversight, electoral transparency, security and opposition accountability remain important public-interest issues.
editorialNote: RadiantWaves Media distinguishes verified developments from statements made by governments, political parties, military authorities and other interested parties. Allegations are attributed to their sources and are not presented as established facts. Figures and investigations may change as authorities publish further information.

breaking.title: Ukraine: Deadly Russian strike hits school being used for aid distribution
breaking.summary: Ukrainian authorities say a Russian bombing struck a school in Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region, which was being used as an aid distribution centre. Authorities reported 24 deaths and approximately 20 people missing as rescue efforts continued.
breaking.content: The attack has renewed international concern about civilian protection in Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemned the strike and said it demonstrated that Moscow was not pursuing de-escalation. The reported casualty figures remain subject to updates as emergency teams continue their work. The Russian government’s response should be considered separately from the Ukrainian authorities' account.

breaking.title: Belgian prime minister offers resignation after budget talks collapse
breaking.summary: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever has offered his resignation after coalition partners failed to reach agreement on the country's 2027 budget.
breaking.content: The dispute followed overnight negotiations involving Belgium's five-party governing coalition. King Philippe has not yet decided whether to accept the resignation. The monarch is expected to consult political leaders before making a decision. Belgium's public finances and rising debt remain central to the political disagreement. The situation creates uncertainty over the government's next steps, but it does not mean a successor has already been appointed.

breaking.title: Strait of Hormuz: Iran makes proposal for reopening as tanker incident raises tensions
breaking.summary: Iranian officials say a two-day proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and resuming nuclear negotiations has been discussed through diplomatic channels. Separately, Iran's Revolutionary Guard has claimed that two tankers caught fire after striking mines.
breaking.content: The tanker incident and the diplomatic proposal have heightened attention on one of the world's most important energy shipping routes. The claim that mines caused the tanker explosions has not been independently established in the reporting cited here. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has referred to contacts with mediators and a proposal involving the reopening of the waterway. The reported Iranian conditions include changes to the US blockade and sanctions arrangements. There is no confirmation in the cited reporting that Washington has accepted the proposal. Any prolonged disruption could affect shipping costs, insurance and international energy markets.

featured.title: Nigeria's electoral register: INEC flags 268 records for further examination
featured.summary: Nigeria's electoral commission says its technology system flagged 268 preliminary voter-register records for suspected irregularities, including photographs believed to have been generated using artificial intelligence.
featured.content: The Independent National Electoral Commission says its Automated Biometric Identification System flagged 268 records for further examination. INEC's ICT Director, Lawrence Bayode, explained that the review includes records with suspected AI-generated photographs and other irregularities. The commission has also explained that some registration cases involve people with incomplete or missing fingers who used a special registration option. This distinction matters: the 268 records have been flagged for review, but that does not mean 268 cases of electoral fraud have been proven. INEC says the preliminary register was displayed for public scrutiny from 26 October, allowing claims and objections to be submitted. The final register is expected to be certified on 15 December. The development has prompted public-interest and political calls for a transparent investigation. Former Kano governor Rabiu Kwankwaso has reportedly called for an independent and thorough examination, with findings made public. The central issue is whether INEC can demonstrate that its register is accurate, inclusive and protected against manipulation before future elections.

topStories.title: Nigeria: Government warns against inflated public contracts
topStories.summary: The Federal Government has warned heads of agencies against inflated contract costs and breaches of public procurement rules.
topStories.content: A circular issued through the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, warns public institutions against procurement practices that undermine competition and transparency. The government has referred to compliance with the Public Procurement Act 2007 and the possibility of sanctions for violations. The public-interest question is how consistently these rules will be enforced and whether investigations and sanctions will be made transparent.

topStories.title: Nigeria: NCDC monitors contacts linked to imported Ebola case
topStories.summary: Health authorities have identified contacts for monitoring following an imported confirmed Ebola case. The monitoring process is a precautionary public-health measure.
topStories.content: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control has reported contact tracing and monitoring following an imported confirmed case. Reports indicate that 62 contacts were identified, with monitoring expected to continue through 13 November. Separately, suspected cases investigated in Adamawa reportedly tested negative after laboratory assessment. These suspected cases should not be confused with confirmed infections. The NCDC remains the appropriate source for official case numbers and public-health guidance.

topStories.title: Civil service reforms focus on productivity and integrity
topStories.summary: Nigeria's Head of Service has described reforms intended to improve efficiency, productivity and public-sector integrity.
topStories.content: The reform discussion places renewed attention on how public institutions deliver services to citizens. Measures aimed at reducing inefficiency and corruption require clear performance standards, transparent procedures and consistent accountability. The practical test will be whether citizens experience improvements in service delivery.

topStories.title: Serbia: Student movement marks anniversary of railway station disaster
topStories.summary: Serbia's student-led political movement continues to draw attention to corruption and accountability following the deadly Novi Sad railway station canopy collapse.
topStories.content: The disaster killed 16 people and became a major focus of public anger and anti-corruption campaigning. Reuters reports that a student-led bloc won 141 of 250 seats in the parliamentary election held on 25 October, defeating the ruling Serbian Progressive Party. The political development is part of a wider debate about public accountability and institutional trust.

topStories.title: Bulgaria: Iliana Yotova leads presidential runoff count
topStories.summary: Bulgaria's public broadcaster reported Iliana Yotova ahead in the presidential runoff based on more than half of tally sheets processed.
topStories.content: With 52.42 per cent of tally sheets processed, the Bulgarian National Television report placed Iliana Yotova on 57.95 per cent and Gyurov on 39.01 per cent. The reported figures represent the count at that stage and should not be confused with final certified results. Further confirmation from the electoral authorities is required before treating the result as final.

articles.title: Why Nigeria's electoral register matters beyond the 268 flagged records
articles.summary: The integrity of an electoral register is fundamental to public confidence in elections. INEC's explanation and the review process deserve careful scrutiny.
articles.content: An electoral register is not simply an administrative list. It determines who can participate in an election and provides the foundation for credible voter participation. The 268 records flagged by INEC should therefore be examined carefully, but the public must not confuse a preliminary alert with proof of wrongdoing. INEC should explain the criteria used to flag records, how genuine registration photographs are distinguished from manipulated images, and how people whose records are affected can challenge an incorrect decision. Political parties and civic organisations also have a responsibility to submit evidence rather than circulate unverified allegations. The process should protect both electoral integrity and the rights of eligible voters. Transparency, independent scrutiny and a clear appeals process can help strengthen confidence before the final register is certified.

articles.title: Nigeria's opposition and the challenge of building public confidence
articles.summary: As Nigeria looks towards its next election cycle, opposition parties face questions about unity, policy credibility, internal democracy and accountability.
articles.content: Nigeria's opposition has an important constitutional role: scrutinising government decisions, presenting alternative policies and offering voters a credible choice. But public frustration alone is not an electoral programme. Political figures including Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi remain part of the wider national opposition conversation, while other political actors and parties also shape the debate. The challenge is whether opposition leaders can move beyond personalities and competing ambitions to explain how they would address insecurity, unemployment, inflation, public debt, electricity, education and healthcare. Electoral integrity must also remain central. Recent questions surrounding INEC's preliminary voter register show why transparent institutions matter to every political party, whether in government or opposition. Calls for independent scrutiny should be accompanied by evidence, due process and respect for eligible voters. Any opposition arrangement will ultimately be judged by the quality of its policies, the credibility of its candidates, its internal democratic standards and its ability to hold itself accountable.

articles.title: Public procurement: A warning is not the same as enforcement
articles.summary: The Federal Government's warning on inflated contracts raises a wider question about transparency and consequences in public spending.
articles.content: Public procurement affects roads, hospitals, schools, security equipment and essential services. Inflated contracts and non-competitive awards can reduce the value citizens receive from public funds. A warning to government agencies is an important administrative step, but effective reform requires open contract information, independent audits, clear conflict-of-interest rules and consequences when violations are established. Citizens should be able to see whether the rules are being applied consistently across institutions.

worldNews.title: Ukraine reports 24 deaths after strike on aid distribution centre
worldNews.summary: Ukrainian authorities say a school being used for aid distribution in Komyshuvakha was hit, with around 20 people still missing at the time of reporting.
worldNews.content: Rescue operations continued after the reported bombing in the Zaporizhzhia region. The casualty figures are attributed to Ukrainian authorities and may change as further information becomes available.

worldNews.title: Middle East: Iran proposal puts Hormuz and nuclear talks back in focus
worldNews.summary: Iran says it has discussed a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume negotiations, while the United States has not confirmed acceptance.
worldNews.content: The proposal reportedly includes conditions involving sanctions, maritime access and a ceasefire. The positions of the parties remain subject to further diplomatic developments.

worldNews.title: Gaza and the occupied West Bank remain under severe pressure
worldNews.summary: Reports from the region describe continued Israeli military operations and Palestinian casualties amid an unstable security situation.
worldNews.content: Al Jazeera's live coverage reported at least nine Palestinians killed across Gaza on Sunday. Its reporting also described continuing Israeli operations in Hebron in the occupied West Bank. Casualty claims and operational details should be attributed to the reporting organisations and relevant authorities as investigations continue.

usaNews.title: United States: Midterm election debate intensifies ahead of voting
usaNews.summary: The approaching US midterm elections have renewed debate about election administration, voter eligibility and political rhetoric.
usaNews.content: A Reuters report examined the Trump administration's efforts to compile and circulate lists of people suspected of being non-citizen voters. State officials challenged aspects of the effort, and legal disputes raised concerns about the possibility of eligible citizens being wrongly affected. Non-citizen voting in federal elections is illegal, but the existence of a list or allegation does not establish that an individual has voted unlawfully. Election authorities must distinguish verified cases from inaccurate records and protect eligible voters' rights.

europeNews.title: Belgium faces government uncertainty after budget dispute
europeNews.summary: Prime Minister Bart De Wever has offered his resignation, but King Philippe has not yet decided whether to accept it.
europeNews.content: The disagreement between coalition partners centres on the 2027 budget and the country's financial position. Consultations with political leaders are expected before a decision.

europeNews.title: France: Protests continue amid pressure over living costs
europeNews.summary: Demonstrations over living costs, fuel, inflation and public services have continued, with reports of mostly peaceful gatherings and smaller clashes in some cities.
europeNews.content: The scale of demonstrations has varied between successive protest days. The debate reflects continuing pressure on household budgets and public services. Protest numbers and incidents should be treated as estimates from the organisations and authorities reporting them.

europeNews.title: Serbia: Anti-corruption movement remains a major political force
europeNews.summary: The student-led movement has gained parliamentary representation following the election reported on 25 October.
europeNews.content: The movement emerged from public anger following the Novi Sad railway station disaster, which killed 16 people. The political debate continues to focus on public accountability and institutional responsibility.

africaNews.title: Nigeria: Electoral register review places INEC under public scrutiny
africaNews.summary: The commission says 268 preliminary records were flagged for examination, prompting calls for transparency and an independent review.
africaNews.content: The review concerns suspected irregularities, including photographs believed to be AI-generated. The records have not all been established as fraudulent. INEC's explanation, public claims process and final certification will be important in assessing the integrity of the register.

africaNews.title: Mauritania: More than 130 migrants rescued off the coast
africaNews.summary: Reports say 134 migrants travelling towards the Canary Islands were rescued off Mauritania.
africaNews.content: The reported group included men, women and children. The incident highlights the continuing risks faced by people attempting dangerous Atlantic crossings. Rescue figures and the circumstances of each operation should be confirmed by the relevant maritime authorities.

nigeriaNews.title: INEC flags 268 preliminary voter records for review
nigeriaNews.summary: The electoral commission says its biometric system identified records requiring further examination, including suspected AI-generated photographs.
nigeriaNews.content: INEC says the flagged records are under review and should not automatically be treated as proven cases of fraud. The commission has opened the preliminary register to public scrutiny and expects final certification on 15 December. Political parties, civil society and eligible voters have a stake in ensuring that genuine registrations are protected and irregular records are addressed transparently.

nigeriaNews.title: Federal Government warns agencies against inflated contracts
nigeriaNews.summary: The government has directed public institutions to comply with procurement rules and warned of sanctions for violations.
nigeriaNews.content: The directive highlights the need for competition, transparency and value for money in government spending. Enforcement and public reporting will be essential to determine whether the warning leads to measurable improvements.

nigeriaNews.title: NCDC continues contact monitoring following imported Ebola case
nigeriaNews.summary: Health authorities are monitoring identified contacts as a precaution following an imported confirmed case.
nigeriaNews.content: The reported 62 contacts are being monitored through the stated follow-up period. Separate suspected cases investigated in Adamawa were reported negative. The public should rely on NCDC updates for confirmed case information and official health advice.

nigeriaNews.title: Opposition faces pressure to turn criticism into a credible programme
nigeriaNews.summary: Nigeria's opposition parties face public questions about unity, policy alternatives and their ability to hold government accountable.
nigeriaNews.content: The next election cycle will test whether opposition parties can present coherent proposals on the economy, security, education, healthcare, electricity and public-sector reform. Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi and other opposition figures remain part of the national political conversation, but this report does not attribute any new statement to them. Voters will need more than campaign slogans: they will need clear policy commitments, realistic implementation plans and transparent records of performance.

asiaNews.title: China's robotics industry shifts attention from movement to artificial intelligence
asiaNews.summary: Chinese robotics companies are increasingly focusing on the intelligence and practical applications of humanoid machines.
asiaNews.content: The next stage of development involves reliability, data, decision-making and the ability to perform useful tasks outside controlled demonstrations. Investment in the sector has been substantial, but commercial deployment remains a challenge.

businessNews.title: Hormuz uncertainty keeps energy shipping risks in focus
businessNews.summary: Developments around the Strait of Hormuz are being closely watched by energy traders, shipping companies and governments.
businessNews.content: The waterway is a strategically important route for global oil and gas shipments. Any prolonged disruption could increase shipping insurance costs, delay cargoes and place pressure on energy prices. Market reactions will depend on the duration of disruption, the availability of alternative routes and diplomatic progress.

businessNews.title: US reportedly discusses possible return of Russian gas flows to Europe
businessNews.summary: A report says US officials have supported discussions about restoring Russian gas exports to Europe through Ukrainian pipelines as part of wider energy diplomacy.
businessNews.content: Reuters reported on a Wall Street Journal account of the proposal but said it could not independently verify the report. The proposal should not be presented as an agreed policy or an implemented deal. Any change in European energy imports would involve major political, commercial and security considerations.

technologyNews.title: Cyberattack targets supermarket refrigeration systems in several European countries
technologyNews.summary: A reported cyber incident affected refrigeration systems at more than 100 stores across several European countries.
technologyNews.content: The Guardian reported that the incident affected retailers in Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Ireland and Estonia. The attackers and their motives have not been established. European officials have expressed concern about deliberate disruption of food-supply infrastructure, while the reporting indicated that food security was not considered at immediate risk. The incident highlights the need for stronger protection of operational technology in essential services.

technologyNews.title: China's robotics firms pursue more capable embodied AI
technologyNews.summary: The robotics industry is moving beyond demonstrations of movement towards machines capable of understanding and completing practical tasks.
technologyNews.content: The next challenge for manufacturers is to make systems reliable, safe and useful in real-world environments. Progress will depend on artificial intelligence, data quality, hardware performance and commercial applications.

editorial.title: Nigeria needs transparent institutions, not political slogans
editorial.summary: The INEC register review and the Federal Government's procurement warning raise a common question: will public institutions be accountable in practice?
editorial.content: Trust in government is built through consistent standards, transparent decisions and consequences when rules are broken. Electoral administration and public procurement may appear to be separate issues, but both affect the relationship between citizens and the state. Nigerians deserve clear explanations, accessible evidence and fair procedures. The same standards should apply to government officials, opposition figures, political parties and public institutions. Accountability should not depend on political loyalty.

analysis.title: Nigeria's opposition: Unity must be built around policy and accountability
analysis.summary: Opposition cooperation may attract public attention, but lasting credibility requires a shared programme and transparent leadership.
analysis.content: Nigeria's political opposition faces a difficult task. Different parties and political figures have their own support bases, ambitions and policy positions. Any cooperation must address how candidates are selected, how disagreements are resolved and how the proposed government would be held accountable. A credible alternative should explain how it would improve security, reduce the cost of living, strengthen electricity supply, create employment and improve public services. It should also explain how it would fund its promises. Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi and other national political figures may feature in public discussions about opposition strategy, but no unverified agreement or alliance should be treated as established. The electorate needs evidence of serious preparation, not simply announcements of political meetings.

analysis.title: The Strait of Hormuz: Why a regional crisis can affect households worldwide
analysis.summary: Disruption to a major shipping route can influence energy costs, transport and the prices paid by consumers.
analysis.content: The economic consequences of a shipping crisis extend beyond the countries directly involved. Oil and gas cargoes, shipping insurance, freight costs and market expectations can all be affected. Governments and businesses will be watching whether diplomatic proposals lead to a sustained reopening of the route. Claims about individual attacks and military developments must be independently checked before they are treated as established facts.

factCheck.title: Fact Check: Have 268 cases of voter fraud been proven in Nigeria?
factCheck.summary: INEC has said that 268 preliminary voter-register records were flagged for further examination. This is not the same as confirming 268 cases of electoral fraud.
factCheck.content: The distinction between a record being flagged and fraud being proven is essential. INEC's explanation refers to suspected irregularities, including photographs believed to be AI-generated. The commission has also discussed special registration arrangements for people with incomplete or missing fingers. The public should wait for the review findings and any formal decisions before describing the records as fraudulent.

factCheck.title: Fact Check: Does a reported tanker explosion prove that the Strait of Hormuz is closed?
factCheck.summary: A reported tanker incident and claims about mines do not by themselves establish that the entire Strait of Hormuz is closed.
factCheck.content: The cited Reuters report attributes the mine claim to Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy. The cause of the reported explosions and the wider status of maritime traffic require independent confirmation. Reports about proposals to reopen the route should also not be confused with confirmation that an agreement has been reached.

beyondStatement.title: Beyond the Statement: What should Nigerians expect from an electoral register review?
beyondStatement.summary: An announcement that records have been flagged is only the beginning. The public needs to understand the evidence, review process and right of appeal.
beyondStatement.content: INEC should explain the technical criteria behind the flagged records, how genuine photographs are distinguished from manipulated images and how affected voters can challenge decisions. Political parties should be able to submit evidence through established procedures. Independent scrutiny can help protect the credibility of the register while preventing eligible voters from being unfairly excluded. The final outcome should be communicated clearly before certification.

publicInterestFeature.title: Public money, public trust: The test of Nigeria's procurement reforms
publicInterestFeature.summary: A government warning against inflated contracts must be followed by transparent procurement records, independent audits and fair enforcement.
publicInterestFeature.content: Public funds are intended to deliver services and infrastructure. When contracts are inflated or awarded without proper competition, citizens may receive less value for the money spent. The Federal Government's warning to agencies is an opportunity to strengthen compliance with procurement law. The public should be able to see whether contract awards are competitive, whether projects are delivered and whether established violations lead to consequences. Accountability should be measured by results, not announcements.

technologyInnovation.title: Artificial intelligence and electoral integrity
technologyInnovation.summary: The INEC review illustrates how AI-generated images can create new challenges for identity verification and voter registration.
technologyInnovation.content: Artificial intelligence can support public services, but synthetic images and manipulated identity material can also complicate verification. Electoral authorities need reliable biometric checks, transparent procedures and safeguards against wrongly rejecting genuine voters. Technology should strengthen public confidence rather than replace due process.

technologyInnovation.title: Cybersecurity for essential services
technologyInnovation.summary: Reported attacks on supermarket refrigeration systems underline the importance of securing operational technology.
technologyInnovation.content: Cybersecurity is no longer limited to computers and office networks. Systems controlling refrigeration, power, transport and industrial equipment can affect public safety and essential services. Organisations need access controls, monitoring, secure backups and tested incident-response plans.

innovation.title: Robotics: The next challenge is practical intelligence
innovation.summary: The robotics industry is increasingly focused on machines that can understand instructions and perform useful tasks reliably.
innovation.content: Demonstrating that a robot can walk or balance is different from proving that it can work safely and consistently in a factory, hospital or home. The next stage requires advances in artificial intelligence, sensors, training data and real-world testing.

leadersWatch.intro: Leaders Watch monitors public decisions, official statements and developments involving influential political figures. No new statement is attributed to a leader unless it is supported by a cited report.

leaders.name: Bola Ahmed Tinubu
leaders.update: Nigeria's electoral register review and the Federal Government's procurement warning remain important governance issues for the administration. No new presidential statement on these specific developments is included in this edition.

leaders.name: Atiku Abubakar
leaders.update: Atiku remains a prominent figure in national opposition discussions. This edition does not attribute a new statement or confirmed alliance to him.

leaders.name: Peter Obi
leaders.update: Obi remains part of the national debate about opposition politics, public accountability and governance. No new statement is attributed to him in this edition.

leaders.name: Rabiu Kwankwaso
leaders.update: The Punch reports that Kwankwaso called for a thorough and transparent investigation into the INEC records flagged for review.

leaders.name: Donald Trump
leaders.update: Trump has made public comments about the conflict involving Iran and the future of the Strait of Hormuz. Statements about the expected end of the conflict should be treated as political claims, not confirmation of a settlement.

leaders.name: Volodymyr Zelenskyy
leaders.update: Zelenskyy condemned the reported strike on the school used as an aid distribution centre in the Zaporizhzhia region.

leaders.name: Bart De Wever
leaders.update: De Wever has offered his resignation following the failure of coalition budget talks. King Philippe has not yet confirmed whether he will accept it.

leaders.name: Emmanuel Macron
leaders.update: France continues to face debate over living costs, public services and political stability. No new presidential statement is attributed in this edition.

leaders.name: Friedrich Merz
leaders.update: Germany remains central to European debates about economic conditions, energy security and regional diplomacy. No new statement is attributed in this edition.

leaders.name: Vladimir Putin
leaders.update: Russia remains central to the war in Ukraine. Ukrainian authorities have attributed the Komyshuvakha strike to Russian forces; the casualty figures are reported by Ukrainian authorities.

leaders.name: Xi Jinping
leaders.update: China's industrial and technology sectors remain under international attention, including developments in robotics and artificial intelligence.

leaders.name: Ursula von der Leyen
leaders.update: European institutions continue to face questions involving energy security, economic resilience and cybersecurity.

leaders.name: Mark Carney
leaders.update: No new verified statement from the Canadian prime minister is included in this edition.

electionWatch.title: Nigeria: Final voter register certification expected in December
electionWatch.summary: INEC says the preliminary register is open to scrutiny and that final certification is expected on 15 December.
electionWatch.content: The 268 flagged records remain under examination. The process should protect the rights of eligible voters while ensuring that irregular records are addressed. Political parties and citizens should use the official claims and objections process.

electionWatch.title: United States: Midterm elections approach amid debate over voter eligibility
electionWatch.summary: Election administration and voter-list accuracy remain prominent issues ahead of voting.
electionWatch.content: Legal and political disputes over suspected non-citizen voter records underline the importance of accurate registration systems and safeguards for eligible citizens. Allegations must be tested against evidence and the law.

breakingHistory.title: Novi Sad railway station disaster: A tragedy that reshaped Serbia's political debate
breakingHistory.summary: The collapse of a railway station canopy killed 16 people and became a focus of public demands for accountability.
breakingHistory.content: The disaster contributed to a student-led anti-corruption movement and a wider debate about public infrastructure, government transparency and institutional responsibility. The anniversary remains a reminder that public safety and accountability must extend beyond political statements.

thoughtForToday.title: Thought for Today
thoughtForToday.quote: A credible democracy is built not only by the leaders who seek power, but by the institutions that hold power accountable.

todaysBigQuestion.title: Today's Big Question
todaysBigQuestion.question: As Nigeria approaches another election cycle, what should voters demand first from political leaders: a credible economic plan, measurable security improvements, a record of public accountability, national unity, or stronger democratic institutions?
todaysBigQuestion.discussion: Public participation should focus on evidence, policies and measurable results rather than political loyalty or personal attacks.

editorialStandards.corrections: Figures and developing stories may change. Corrections should be made when reliable new information becomes available.
